thread:
maya: Quick ping — FinEdge wants an EU-only POC next week. Their checklist: inference traffic, logs, metrics, debug dumps must not leave EU. Can we confirm Hosted vs Dedicated guarantees and a short checklist I can send?

sam: Hosted can prefer EU endpoints but we do have a few control-plane subprocessors that may reach outside EU for analytics/aggregates. Dedicated can be provisioned EU-only with VPC and optional private control plane — much stronger.

sam: Example tenant config snippet I use for sales:
```yaml
routing:
  preferred_region: eu-west-1
  tenant_pin: true
  egress_policy: eu-only
  fallback_policy: reject
```

liam: Quick subproc note for Hosted EU: AWS eu-west-1 (compute/storage), Datadog EU shard (metrics), Sentry EU shard (PII-scrubbed errors), ObservabilityProv (EU contract). There are small aggregate analytics jobs that post outside EU — limited but present. If they require zero non-EU subprocessors, recommend Dedicated/Private.

liam: Subprocessor inventory link: https://redwood.example.com/subproc-inventory#eu

carla: Legal: we can share SCCs and a current subprocessor list for presales POCs. Formal attestation (signed SOC/ISO pack or explicit PoA) requires collecting vendor docs — plan for ~2-3 weeks. Dedicated shortens the exposure surface (BYOK/KMS scoped to region).

maya: They also asked about pricing and minimum commitment for a Dedicated trial. Is there a standard offer?

sam: Options to propose:
- Hosted with EU preferences: fastest, lowest cost, not certified EU-only for control-plane items.
- Short Dedicated trial (1-2 weeks): ops approval required, small provisioning fee; we can apply credits on a case-by-case basis.
- Private/on-prem: longest lead and highest effort.

ops-bot: Ticket INC-9987 created for EU Dedicated warmup. Typical warmup 48-72h after approval.

infra-eng: If fallback_policy=reject we will reject requests when EU capacity is exhausted (use language: "requests will be rejected when EU capacity unavailable"). If fallback_policy=nearest we may route to a compatible non-EU variant. For POC we can set reject.

maya: We need one plain SOW sentence describing what stays in EU vs what may leave. Can someone draft a clear line?

liam: Draft SOW sentence: "All request payloads, model inputs and outputs, and per-request logs will be stored and processed only within EU regions. Aggregated, non-identifiable operational metrics and product analytics may be processed outside the EU unless Dedicated or Private deployment is selected."

carla: That reads fine. Add: "Customer may request a subprocessor attestation; delivery timeline 2-3 weeks depending on vendor responsiveness." Legal will start pulling vendor docs after sales confirms.

maya: Draft POC checklist I'll send to FinEdge:
- Choose deployment: Hosted (note control-plane caveats) or Dedicated (EU-only option).
- Approve egress_policy (reject vs nearest).
- Complete security questionnaire + provide PO contact.
- Confirm BYOK/KMS requirement (yes/no).
- Review and approve allowed sub-processors (link attached).
- Sign POC scope & ops kickoff (include warmup window and provisioning fee).
- Confirm whether request-level encryption keys are required.

sam: Also clarify expected SLA for the trial (best-effort) and whether they want logging redaction or full logs retained in EU.

carla: We'll prepare SCC copies and the subproc list. ETA for an initial attestation packet ~10 business days if vendors respond quickly.

maya: Thanks all — I'll send the checklist and flag that a formal attestation may follow. Tagging @carla for legal attestation and @infra-eng for capacity confirmation.

participants: maya, sam, liam, carla, ops-bot, infra-eng
